All three are live and verified. Here's the last core exploration.

First, the shared part in all three: a **filter** at the top — **All / To read / Finished**, each showing a count — so you can focus the list. And an important reassurance: marking something *finished* never deletes it; it just moves between views, so useful links are always kept.

Please open each version, try **changing one card's status**, and watch it move when you switch the filter:

- **Version A — a round check button on each card:** http://maker:4001/status-a.html
  *(click the circle to mark a card read; click again to send it back to "To read")*
- **Version B — the status tag itself is the toggle:** http://maker:4001/status-b.html
  *(click the "Read later" / "Read ✓" tag on a card to flip it — no extra control)*
- **Version C — an explicit "Mark as read" button:** http://maker:4001/status-c.html
  *(a clearly labelled button that names exactly what it'll do)*

In each, also click the **To read** and **Finished** tabs at the top to see the list focus.

A few decisions I'd like you to judge:
- **The three views** — All / To read / Finished — are those the right buckets and names, or would you frame them differently?
- **Finished cards look slightly dimmed** so your eye goes to what's still pending. Does that feel right, or should finished links look identical to the rest?

So two questions for you: **which way of changing status feels most natural (A, B, or C)**, and **does the filter give you the "focus on what's left to read" you wanted?**
